FCPD: Speed, alcohol likely factors in fatal Little River Turnpike crash

By Angela Woolsey
Published November 16, 2026 at 8:30AM
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:33
Instaread

A Burke man died this weekend after crashing his car during an early-morning drive on Little River Turnpike in Annandale, police say.

Officers were dispatched at around 2:16 a.m. on Saturday (Nov. 14) to the single-vehicle crash on Little River Turnpike near the Capital Beltway (I-495) overpass.

According to the Fairfax County Police Department, a preliminary investigation suggests 28-year-old Christian Bejarano was heading east on Little River Turnpike in a Subaru Impreza “when his vehicle left the roadway and struck a guardrail.”

Transported to a hospital with injuries described by police as life-threatening, he was pronounced dead. Bejarano was the only person in the vehicle at the time of the crash, the FCPD noted.

“Preliminarily, speed and alcohol are believed to be factors in the crash,” the FCPD said later that day in a press release. “Detectives are continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding the crash.”

Bejarano is the 48th person to die in a crash in Fairfax County this year by FFXnow’s count. The Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles’ traffic database currently lists 44 fatalities for 2026 based on preliminary police reports, but two deaths in October, a Nov. 10 crash that ultimately killed a teenage pedestrian outside Chantilly High School and the Nov. 14 crash on Little River Turnpike don’t appear to have been included yet.

This is the second fatal crash to occur on Little River Turnpike in 2026, following a June 19 incident where a Honda Civic driver struck and killed a 73-year-old pedestrian at the Southland Avenue intersection in Lincolnia.
